context:
Treat Result Detail as a detail/receipt surface, not a dense leaderboard
surface. Preserve compact shared formatting where it improves scanning, but
expose exact power-score evidence where users inspect a single result.
description:
The follow-up remediation release gate caught a post-merge regression in the
full Results Explorer frontend suite. `ResultDetail.test.tsx` now fails after
the shared metric-formatting rollout because the canonical result summary no
longer exposes exact power-score precision, and the median/raw duration table
contract no longer matches the rendered labels.

This is a release-blocking evidence issue, not just stale tests: Result
Detail is the route where users inspect an individual benchmark receipt, so
compact leaderboard/table formatting must not erase exact score evidence or
make raw timing units ambiguous.

anti_patterns.dont: add source changes outside Result Detail, shared formatter helpers, or focused tests unless reproduction proves the issue is shared.
silence the failing tests without deciding the detail-route contract.

preserves.behavior: Leaderboard, benchmark, platform, query, and compare surfaces must keep compact large power-score formatting.
Raw sort/comparison values must remain numeric and unrounded.
Result Detail must preserve exact score evidence for receipt-level inspection.
Timing headers must match the rendered timing unit contract.

prior_art.concept: results-explorer/src/lib/metricFormatters.ts centralizes compact/exact power score and dynamic latency formatting.
results-explorer/src/pages/ResultDetail.tsx owns the result summary, median display-timing table, and expanded raw query table.
results-explorer/src/pages/__tests__/ResultDetail.test.tsx contains the failing median-first and exact score precision contract tests.

verifications.description: Result Detail formatter regression tests pass
Full Results Explorer frontend suite passes

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run typecheck && npm run build

work_units.notes:
Result Detail should expose exact power-score precision in the canonical
result summary or an equally explicit detail-only affordance. Do not revert
compact score formatting on leaderboards, benchmark/platform tables, or
compare cards.
work_units.summary: Restore exact result-summary score evidence without reintroducing noisy dense-table decimals

work_units.notes:
The default median table and expanded raw-query table must have headers that
agree with their values. If values use dynamic `ms`/`s` formatting, use
semantic headers such as `Median latency` and `Duration`; if raw table
values are guaranteed milliseconds, keep explicit `(ms)` copy.
work_units.summary: Align median/raw duration labels with the displayed timing units
